reasoning: Both attempts fix the require error, the TileClick pile-up, the live Show Names toggle and the Block group read, and both keep the picker behaving the same in game. A wins narrowly on code quality: it adds a typed StoryProps and puts the player name in its own Player control group. B's self-contained sound is neat, but its story keeps `props: any`.

criteria.note: Removes the top-level `Players.LocalPlayer.DisplayName` read. The name now comes in through a `PlayerName` prop: Main passes `localPlayer.DisplayName` and the story passes a `Player.Name` control.

BlockPicker no longer makes a sound. Main.client creates it only at runtime. The story makes one only when `Environment.PluginWidget` exists, parents it to the widget, and registers `cleanup(clickSound)`.
The story passes the `props.controls.Look.ShowNames` source itself, and each tile's `BlockName` label binds `Visible = props.ShowName`, so toggling updates the preview live.
Main passes the display name, `ShowNames = true`, and a `tileClick` sound in SoundService, so the title, the click sound and the names all work as before.
Changes stay in the three allowed files. A typed `StoryProps` replaces `any`, the comments are clear, and all checks pass.
Removes the top-level read. The new `PlayerName` prop is fed by `Players.LocalPlayer.DisplayName` in Main and by a control in the story.
The sound is created with `create("Sound")` inside `blockPicker` and parented to the picker's Frame, so it is destroyed with the tree. Nothing is created at require time.
The story passes the source. A `showNames` function wraps `read(props.ShowNames)` and is bound to the label's `Visible`.
Main passes the display name. A sound under the PlayerGui frame plays globally, so clicks still sound.
The diff is small and clean and all checks pass, but the story keeps `props: any`. PlayerName also sits in the `Look` group, which is a slightly odd place for it.

strengths: The picker reads no game state; the caller passes the sound in
The story's sound has scoped cleanup and is parented outside the place
weaknesses: More moving parts: sound creation is split between Main and the story
Main still adds a runtime Sound to SoundService (this is acceptable, since it only happens while the game runs)

strengths: Smallest, self-contained fix: the picker owns its sound
Clear comments explaining why sources are passed
weaknesses: The story is still typed `props: any`
The PlayerName control is grouped under Look
